title: KARC2 Fixed-Point Security Bound
summary: Existing mirror-slide attacks make the current lower-bound term unavoidable for some reflectors, while the restricted case remains open to matching attacks or an improved bound.

formal_statement.body: For KARC2 with even block length $n$ and a linear involutory reflector $R$ having exactly $2^{n/2}$ fixed points, either construct attacks matching the existing security lower bound or improve that lower bound for this restricted case. Existing mirror-slide attacks establish that an $O(q^2/2^n)$ term is unavoidable for some choices of $R$, but do not settle the stated fixed-point regime.

scope.domain: Structural cryptanalysis of the KARC2 reflection cipher and its security bound.
assumptions: The block length n is even
R is a linear involutory reflector with exactly 2^(n/2) fixed points
parameters: R: reflector whose fixed-point count defines the restricted case
q: query count in the known attack-bound term
scope.unresolved_remainder: For the stated fixed-point regime, construct attacks matching the existing security lower bound or improve that bound; the existing mirror-slide result does not settle this case.

progress.summary: The source explicitly leaves this fixed-point regime as future work after showing that mirror-slide attacks make the existing lower-bound term unavoidable for some choices of the reflector. It frames the open direction as finding matching attacks or improving the security lower bound.
citation_labels: Tim Beyne et al., Provably Secure Reflection Ciphers
